title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 35.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 35, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Josiah kept a passover unto the LORD in Jerusalem
Josiah gave to the people lambs and kids for the passover offerings
Josiah set the priests in their charges and encouraged them
Josiah told the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah kept a passover unto the LORD in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:1 states that Josiah kept a passover unto the LORD in Jerusalem at the beginning of the chapter.

questions.question: Who did Josiah set in their charges and encouraged to the service of the house of the LORD?
options: The rulers of the house of God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:2 says Josiah set the priests in their charges and encouraged them to the service of the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What did Josiah tell the Levites to do with the holy ark?
options: Put the holy ark in the house Solomon built
Carry the holy ark on their shoulders
Hide the holy ark from the people
Take the holy ark to the temple of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Put the holy ark in the house Solomon built
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:3 instructs the Levites to put the holy ark in the house which Solomon built.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 35, how were the Levites to prepare themselves?
options: By the houses of their fathers, after their courses
questions.correctAnswer: By the houses of their fathers, after their courses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:4 states that the Levites should prepare themselves by the houses of their fathers, after their courses.

questions.question: Where were the Levites instructed to stand according to their divisions?
options: In the courts of the king
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:5 says the Levites were to stand in the holy place according to the divisions of their families.

questions.question: What were the people instructed to do with the passover according to the word of the LORD?
options: Kill the passover and sanctify themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Kill the passover and sanctify themselves
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:6 commands to kill the passover and sanctify themselves to prepare their brethren as per the LORD's word.

questions.question: How many lambs and kids did Josiah give for the passover offerings?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:7 states Josiah gave lambs and kids to the number of thirty thousand for the passover offerings.

questions.question: How many bullocks did Josiah provide from the king's substance for the passover?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:7 notes that Josiah provided three thousand bullocks of the king's substance for the passover.

questions.question: Who among the following gave willingly unto the people, priests, and Levites for the passover offerings?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:8 states that Josiah's princes gave willingly unto the people, priests, and Levites for the passover offerings.

questions.question: How many small cattle did Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel give for the passover offerings?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:8 reports that Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel gave two thousand and six hundred small cattle for the passover offerings.

questions.question: How many oxen did the rulers of the house of God give for the passover offerings?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:8 states the rulers of the house of God gave three hundred oxen for the passover offerings.

questions.question: Did Conaniah, Shemaiah, Nethaneel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad give cattle for the passover offerings?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:9 confirms that Conaniah, Shemaiah, Nethaneel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad gave cattle for the passover offerings.

questions.question: Did Josiah command to prepare the brethren so they may do according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:6 says Josiah instructed to prepare the brethren that they may do according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses.

questions.question: Josiah gave five thousand oxen for the passover offerings.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:7-9 shows Josiah gave three thousand bullocks and the Levites and rulers gave five hundred and three hundred oxen respectively, not Josiah himself giving five thousand oxen.

questions.question: The chapter says Josiah instructed the Levites to carry the holy ark on their shoulders.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:3 states Josiah told the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built so it would not be a burden on their shoulders, not to carry it.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who killed the passover according to 2 Chronicles 35:11?
questions.explanation: The priests killed the passover as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:11.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 35:12 promise will happen if someone follows the instruction to remove burnt offerings?
options: They will offer to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will offer to the LORD
questions.explanation: Following the instruction leads to the offering unto the LORD as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:12.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 35:14, why did the Levites prepare for themselves and the priests?
options: Because they had to leave early
Because they were not allowed to serve
questions.explanation: The Levites prepared for themselves and the priests because the priests were occupied with the offerings until night, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 35:14.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 35:15 indicate about the singers and porters?
options: They were allowed to leave early
They were in their places as commanded
questions.correctAnswer: They were in their places as commanded
questions.explanation: The singers and porters were in their designated places according to the commandment of David, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:15.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 35:16, what was prepared on the same day to keep the passover?
questions.explanation: The service of the LORD was prepared on that day to keep the passover, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 35:16.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do according to 2 Chronicles 35:17?
questions.explanation: The children of Israel that were present kept the passover and the feast of unleavened bread, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:17.

questions.question: What is noted about the passover kept by Josiah in 2 Chronicles 35:18?
options: It was the greatest passover in Israel's history
It was kept in a different location
questions.correctAnswer: It was the greatest passover in Israel's history
questions.explanation: There was no passover like that kept in Israel from the days of Samuel, indicating its significance, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:18.

questions.question: How many lambs and kids did Josiah give for the passover offerings according to 2 Chronicles 35:7?
questions.explanation: Josiah gave thirty thousand lambs and kids for the passover offerings, as noted in 2 Chronicles 35:7.

questions.question: What were the Levites instructed to do according to 2 Chronicles 35:3?
options: Put the holy ark in the house
questions.correctAnswer: Put the holy ark in the house
questions.explanation: The Levites were instructed to put the holy ark in the house built by Solomon, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:3.

questions.question: What did the princes give for the passover offerings according to 2 Chronicles 35:8?
questions.explanation: The princes gave willingly to the priests for the passover offerings, as noted in 2 Chronicles 35:8.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Levites' preparation according to 2 Chronicles 35:14?
questions.explanation: The Levites prepared for themselves and the priests because the priests were busy with offerings, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:14.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 35:6, what did the people need to do before they killed the passover?
questions.explanation: The instruction was to sanctify themselves before killing the passover, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:6.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 35:10, who stood in their place during the service?
questions.explanation: The priests and Levites stood in their place as per the king's command, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:10.

questions.question: The children of Israel did not keep the passover as commanded in 2 Chronicles 35:17.
questions.explanation: The children of Israel that were present kept the passover at that time, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:17.

questions.question: The Levites were not involved in the passover offerings according to 2 Chronicles 35:12.
questions.explanation: The Levites were actively involved in the offerings, as stated in 2 Chronicles 35:12.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 35.

questions.question: In which year of Josiah's reign was the Passover kept according to 2 Chronicles 35?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:19 states, 'In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah was this passover kept.'

questions.question: Who came up to fight against Carchemish, prompting Josiah to go out against him?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:20 identifies Necho king of Egypt as the one who came up to fight against Carchemish.

questions.question: What reason did Necho give for not wanting Josiah to interfere?
options: God commanded me to make haste and forbade you meddling with Him
Josiah was to be an ally, not an enemy
It was a personal matter unrelated to Judah
questions.correctAnswer: God commanded me to make haste and forbade you meddling with Him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:21 shows Necho sending ambassadors saying God commanded him to make haste and to forbear Josiah from meddling with God who was with him.

questions.question: How did Josiah respond to Necho's warning?
options: He disguised himself and went to fight
He turned back and did not engage
questions.correctAnswer: He disguised himself and went to fight
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:22 states Josiah did not heed Necho's words but disguised himself to fight in the valley of Megiddo.

questions.question: What happened to Josiah during the battle at Megiddo?
options: He was sore wounded by archers' arrows
questions.correctAnswer: He was sore wounded by archers' arrows
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:23 records that archers shot at Josiah and he told his servants he was sore wounded.

questions.question: Who lamented for Josiah after his death according to 2 Chronicles 35?
options: Jeremiah and the singing men and women
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah and the singing men and women
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:25 says Jeremiah lamented for Josiah and the singing men and women spoke of him in their lamentations.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Megiddo' in 2 Chronicles 35:22 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew name 'Megiddo' (מְגִדּוֹ) is traditionally understood as 'place of assembly' or 'meeting place', as seen in 2 Chronicles 35:22.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 35:19-24 describing Josiah’s last battle?
questions.explanation: The narrative foreshadows Josiah's death by first highlighting his faithfulness and then his tragic end in battle (2 Chronicles 35:19-24), a literary device preparing readers for the decline of Judah.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Josiah’s reform and covenant renewal as described in 2 Chronicles 35?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 speaks of God’s new covenant written on hearts, echoing Josiah’s renewal of the covenant and law (2 Chronicles 35:26).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Josiah’s Passover in 2 Chronicles 35:1-19 in terms of the Passover celebration?
questions.explanation: Exodus 12 details the institution of the Passover, which Josiah restored in 2 Chronicles 35:1-19, showing continuity with Mosaic law.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Josiah's confrontation with Necho in 2 Chronicles 35?
options: The writing of the book of the law
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:19-20 shows that after Josiah kept the Passover, Necho came up and Josiah went out against him.

questions.question: What typological significance does Josiah’s death in 2 Chronicles 35:23-24 hold in biblical theology?
options: A foreshadowing of the Messiah's suffering
A symbol of Israel's ultimate victory
An example of divine blessing for kingship
questions.correctAnswer: A foreshadowing of the Messiah's suffering
questions.explanation: Josiah’s death after faithful service and reform foreshadows the suffering servant motif fulfilled in the Messiah (2 Chronicles 35:23-24).

questions.question: How does the parallelism in 2 Chronicles 35:25 emphasize Josiah’s impact on Israel?
options: By showing both men and women lamenting him equally
By contrasting Josiah with his predecessors
By repeating the phrase 'lamentations to this day'
By listing all the cities mourning him
questions.correctAnswer: By showing both men and women lamenting him equally
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:25 uses parallelism by mentioning both singing men and women lamenting Josiah, highlighting his broad impact.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 35:27, Josiah’s deeds are recorded only in the book of the kings of Judah.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:27 states Josiah’s deeds are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, not only Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Josiah hearkened to the words of Necho who claimed to speak by God in 2 Chronicles 35.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:22 explicitly says Josiah hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of God.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 35:6 teach about sanctification in relation to God's covenant?
options: Sanctification involves preparing oneself and others to obey the word of the LORD as revealed through Moses
Sanctification is an instantaneous act without ongoing preparation
Sanctification is solely a priestly function unrelated to the people
Sanctification is achieved by external ritual only without inner transformation
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves preparing oneself and others to obey the word of the LORD as revealed through Moses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:6 commands to sanctify themselves and prepare others to do according to the word of the LORD by Moses, showing sanctification requires active obedience and preparation.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 35:27?
options: God's covenant faithfulness is recorded and remembered through the history of kings of Israel and Judah
God's covenant is conditional and can be erased from history
God's faithfulness is irrelevant to the deeds of kings
God’s covenant is limited only to the temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant faithfulness is recorded and remembered through the history of kings of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:27 states Josiah’s deeds are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, indicating God's faithfulness is preserved in covenant history.

questions.question: What doctrine about human responsibility before God does 2 Chronicles 35:22 illustrate?
options: Human responsibility includes obedience to divine warnings even in the face of conflict
Humans are free to reject divine warnings without consequence
Divine warnings are optional and symbolic only
Human responsibility is only communal, not individual
questions.correctAnswer: Human responsibility includes obedience to divine warnings even in the face of conflict
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:22 shows Josiah disregarded Necho’s warning, which came with a claim of God’s command, illustrating human responsibility to heed divine warnings.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 35:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:21 shows Necho acting under God's command indicating God’s sovereign control over nations and events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 35:18 regarding the celebration of the Passover?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 35:18 emphasizes a unique, holy celebration of the Passover unlike any other, reflecting God's call to holiness in worship.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 35:1-19 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant renewal?
options: The detailed celebration of the Passover represents a renewal of the covenant relationship between God and Israel
Passover is unrelated to covenant and is purely a historical festival
The chapter emphasizes political alliances over covenant
This chapter rejects covenant renewal in favor of ritual formalism
questions.correctAnswer: The detailed celebration of the Passover represents a renewal of the covenant relationship between God and Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 1-19 describe Josiah’s Passover which recalls covenant faithfulness and renewal through obedience and worship, a key biblical theme.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 35:20-24 fulfill redemptive-historical themes about kingship and divine judgment?
options: Josiah’s death after disobedience to God’s warning illustrates the consequences of rejecting God’s authority
Josiah’s death is unrelated to his relationship with God
The king is invincible regardless of obedience
Divine judgment is arbitrary and disconnected from human action
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah’s death after disobedience to God’s warning illustrates the consequences of rejecting God’s authority
questions.explanation: Josiah’s refusal to heed the divine warning from Necho leads to his death, demonstrating biblical themes of judgment tied to kingship and obedience.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 35:7 and 2 Chronicles 35:8 teach about God's provision and human stewardship?
options: God provides abundantly and human leaders are called to steward and distribute offerings willingly
God’s provision is limited and humans must compete for resources
Offerings are a burden and not connected to God’s provision
Human stewardship is optional and unrelated to God's blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God provides abundantly and human leaders are called to steward and distribute offerings willingly
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 show Josiah and his princes giving large numbers of animals for the Passover, illustrating God’s abundant provision and human responsibility in stewardship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 35:11 and 2 Chronicles 35:13 teach about ritual worship and community participation?
options: Proper ritual worship involves both priestly duties and communal sharing of offerings
Rituals are performed only by priests without community involvement
Community participation is independent of ritual worship
Ritual worship excludes the Levites and people
questions.correctAnswer: Proper ritual worship involves both priestly duties and communal sharing of offerings
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 13 describe priests killing and sprinkling blood, Levites preparing offerings, and sharing them rapidly among the people, indicating communal participation is integral.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 35:14 and 2 Chronicles 35:15 teach about the integration of worship elements in temple service?
options: Worship is a coordinated effort involving priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers according to divine order
Worship is a spontaneous, uncoordinated act
Only priests are involved in worship, excluding musicians and gatekeepers
Temple service is purely ritualistic without musical or organizational elements
questions.correctAnswer: Worship is a coordinated effort involving priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers according to divine order
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 show the priests busy with offerings, Levites preparing, and singers and gatekeepers maintaining their posts, illustrating ordered, integrated worship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 35:20-24 portrays Josiah's death as unjust punishment. What does the text actually teach?
options: Josiah disobeyed the divine warning and thus faced consequences, showing just divine judgment
Josiah was killed arbitrarily without reason
The text portrays Josiah as sinless but tragically punished
Josiah’s death is unrelated to divine will
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah disobeyed the divine warning and thus faced consequences, showing just divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 20-24 narrate Josiah’s refusal to heed Necho’s divinely given warning, resulting in his death, illustrating the justice of divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 35:3 teach about the holiness of the ark and God's presence among His people?
options: The ark is holy and must not be a burden, symbolizing God's sanctified presence dwelling properly among the people
The ark is an ordinary object without holiness
The ark can be carried anywhere without concern
God’s presence is not connected with the ark
questions.correctAnswer: The ark is holy and must not be a burden, symbolizing God's sanctified presence dwelling properly among the people
questions.explanation: Verse 3 commands placing the holy ark in the temple so it won’t be a burden, reflecting the ark’s holiness and God’s proper presence among Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 35:25 specifically demonstrate through Jeremiah’s lamentations for Josiah?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 shows Jeremiah and others lamenting Josiah, making ordinances that preserve his memory, reflecting God’s merciful remembrance of His servants.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 35:4-5 teach about the doctrine of priestly and Levitical order in worship?
options: Worship must be conducted in an ordered manner according to family divisions and established courses
Worship can be conducted randomly without prescribed order
There is no distinction among priests and Levites in worship
Order in worship is a human invention not commanded by God
questions.correctAnswer: Worship must be conducted in an ordered manner according to family divisions and established courses
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 instruct Levites to stand in their divisions and according to family courses, affirming divinely mandated order in worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 35:16 and 2 Chronicles 35:17 teach about covenant renewal and communal worship?
options: The Passover and Feast of Unleavened Bread together foster communal covenant renewal and obedience
The feast is an optional cultural festival unrelated to covenant
Community worship is less important than individual sacrifice
The feast is purely historical with no present theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: The Passover and Feast of Unleavened Bread together foster communal covenant renewal and obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 17 show the Passover and seven-day feast kept by all Israel, symbolizing corporate renewal of covenant and obedience to God.
